q: Name a POSIX or Linux signal.

answers.l: Signal 9. Cannot be caught, blocked or ignored. The kernel just ends you.
Signal 15, kill's default. A polite request to clean up and exit.
Signal 2. What Ctrl-C sends.
Signal 1. Born when modems hung up. Daemons reuse it to mean "reload your config."
Signal 11. Segmentation fault: you touched memory you do not own.
Like SIGKILL, it cannot be caught. Pauses the process until SIGCONT.
Sent when a child exits. Ignore it and you collect zombies.
Writing to a pipe with no reader. Why `yes | head -1` exits quietly.
Yours to define. dd prints progress on it; nginx reopens log files.
Also yours to define. Many servers use it for zero-downtime binary upgrades.
Signal 6. What abort() and failed assertions raise.
Signal 14. Delivered when an alarm() timer expires.
Ctrl-\. Quits with a core dump. The JVM prints a thread dump instead.
Ctrl-Z. The catchable cousin of SIGSTOP.
Resumes a stopped process. fg and bg send it.
Bus error: misaligned access, or touching an mmap’d file that shrank.
Floating-point exception, also raised for integer division by zero despite the name.
Illegal instruction. Often an AVX binary on a CPU without AVX.
Debugger breakpoints. On x86, the int3 instruction raises it.
Window changed: your terminal was resized. How vim and less redraw.
Bad system call. seccomp filters can raise it.
A background job tried to read from the terminal.
A background job tried to write to the terminal (with tostop set).
Urgent socket data. Go 1.14 borrowed it for asynchronous goroutine preemption, since almost nobody uses it.
CPU time limit exceeded (RLIMIT_CPU).
File size limit exceeded (RLIMIT_FSIZE).
Profiling timer. Sampling profilers like pprof tick on it.
Virtual timer: counts only time spent in user mode.
Asynchronous I/O is possible. Also known as SIGPOLL.
System V name for pollable events. Linux aliases it to SIGIO.
Power failure. A UPS daemon sends it to init.
Stack fault on a coprocessor. Defined on Linux, essentially never sent.
BSD and macOS: Ctrl-T asks a process for a status report. Linux never adopted it.
An old synonym for SIGABRT, named for the PDP-11's IOT instruction.
The first real-time signal. Queued, ordered, and able to carry data.

nope.eof: Ctrl-D is not a signal. The terminal just ends the input.

traps.q: Name the signal that can never be caught, blocked or ignored, and is not SIGSTOP.
Name the signal that kill sends when you give it no signal at all.
